fullPassage:
My grandparents sell their delicious organic jam at the local market every weekend. I went to help them last weekend. However, they had already sold all of their jam! They didn't have enough strawberries to make any more jam. That evening, I sat by the window and stared out at the empty field behind their house. Suddenly, I got an idea. The field would be the perfect place for a larger greenhouse. Then they could grow more strawberries! I immediately started searching for a way, and I found the perfect solution. I would start a crowdfunding campaign!

Crowdfunding is a way of raising money for a product, company, or charity. These days, people can use crowdfunding websites to collect money. Crowdfunding is especially advantageous for individuals or small companies that can't attract big investors. If the campaign is successful, the investors receive direct rewards for their contribution.

My grandparents were thrilled when I told them my idea. With the help of investors, we could build a large greenhouse and grow a lot more strawberries. Moreover, we could reward the investors for their help by sending them jars of organic jam! With this plan in mind, the next step was to figure out the details.

Before beginning your campaign, be sure to plan all the production details. How many products will you make? How long will it take to make the product? This planning is important because your potential investors will want to see a clear schedule. Once your plan is complete, remember to set your funding goal. It should be enough to complete the project and fulfill the rewards for the investors. Consider all the necessary costs before deciding on the amount.

After doing some calculations, we decided on an 8-by-12-foot greenhouse. We thought it would cost approximately $4,000. Once it was built, we could fill it with strawberry plants and expect a harvest within about four months. Then it would take a few weeks to turn the strawberries into delicious jam. We decided to set our funding goal at $5,000 to cover all the costs. Also, we planned to run the campaign for three months. I was really excited when I filled out the form to launch the campaign. In less than a week, our application was accepted and funding began!

For a successful crowdfunding campaign, promoting it is necessary. You should consider making a video. This allows investors to get to know you and learn about your product. In the video, describe your situation clearly and show your product. You also need to express how important the product is to you. Don't forget to include a direct request for support at the end.

During a campaign, it is important to send investors updates every week. Through the update, the investors will be able to track the progress of the campaign.

After our application was accepted, I was eager to make a good first impression with our investors. To achieve this, I made a video about my grandparents and their jam. In the video, I highlighted how the strawberries were grown without using chemicals. I also included clips of my grandparents. In the clips, they were making the jam with all-natural ingredients. Finally, I explained where I wanted to put the new greenhouse and asked for support. After some editing, I posted the video on many social media sites. It didn't take long for word of our campaign to spread.

Funding for our campaign started slowly. When the first investor committed to supporting us, I almost jumped for joy. Now, after six weeks, we have raised almost $2,500. It seems like we might make our funding goal!

questions.passage: I would start a crowdfunding campaign! Crowdfunding is a way of raising money for a product, company, or charity. These days, people can use crowdfunding websites to collect money. Crowdfunding is especially (A)[advantageous / disadvantageous] for individuals or small companies that can't attract big investors. If the campaign is (B)[successful / unsuccessful], the investors receive direct (C)[rewards / penalties] for their contribution. My grandparents were thrilled when I told them my idea.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 크라우드펀딩은 제품, 회사, 자선 단체를 위해 돈을 모금하는 방식이다. 크라우드펀딩은 큰 투자자를 끌어들일 수 없는 개인이나 작은 회사에 특히 유리하다. 캠페인이 성공적이면 투자자들은 기여에 대한 직접적인 보상을 받는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ① advantageous – successful – rewards
❌ ② ② disadvantageous – successful – penalties
❌ ③ ③ advantageous – unsuccessful – rewards
❌ ④ ④ disadvantageous – unsuccessful – penalties
✅ (A) advantageous: 큰 투자자를 못 끌어들이는 이들에게 '유리한' 대안.
✅ (B) successful: 캠페인이 '성공'하면 보상을 받는다.
✅ (C) rewards: 기여에 대한 '보상'을 받는다.
det.tip: advantageous(유리한) ↔ disadvantageous(불리한) / reward(보상) ↔ penalty(처벌)

questions.passage: Before beginning your campaign, be sure to plan all the production details. This planning is important because your (A)[potential / actual] investors will want to see a clear schedule. Once your plan is complete, remember to set your funding goal. It should be enough to complete the project and (B)[fulfill / ignore] the rewards for the investors. Consider all the (C)[necessary / unnecessary] costs before deciding on the amount.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 캠페인 시작 전 모든 생산 세부 사항을 계획해라. 잠재적인 투자자들이 명확한 일정을 보고 싶어 할 것이다. 프로젝트를 완료하고 보상을 충족시킬 정도로 충분해야 한다. 필요한 모든 비용을 고려해라.
det.analysis:
❌ ① ① actual – fulfill – unnecessary
❌ ② ② potential – ignore – necessary
❌ ③ ③ actual – ignore – unnecessary
✅ ④ ④ potential – fulfill – necessary
✅ (A) potential: 아직 투자하지 않은 '잠재적' 투자자.
✅ (B) fulfill: 보상을 '충족시키다'. ignore(무시하다)는 반대.
✅ (C) necessary: '필요한' 비용. unnecessary는 반대.
det.tip: potential(잠재적인) ↔ actual(실제의) / fulfill(충족하다) ↔ ignore(무시하다)

questions.passage: For a successful crowdfunding campaign, (A)[promoting / neglecting] it is necessary. You should consider making a video. This allows investors to get to know you and learn about your product. In the video, describe your situation clearly and show your product. You also need to express how (B)[important / irrelevant] the product is to you. Don't forget to include a (C)[direct / indirect] request for support at the end.
questions.stem: 위 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 성공적인 캠페인을 위해 홍보하는 것이 필요하다. 제품이 당신에게 얼마나 중요한지 표현해야 한다. 마지막에는 지원에 대한 직접적인 요청을 포함해라.
det.analysis:
✅ ① ① promoting – important – direct
❌ ② ② neglecting – important – indirect
❌ ③ ③ promoting – irrelevant – direct
❌ ④ ④ neglecting – irrelevant – indirect
✅ (A) promoting: 캠페인 홍보가 필요. neglecting(방치)은 반대.
✅ (B) important: 제품의 중요성 표현. irrelevant(무관한)은 반대.
✅ (C) direct: '직접적인' 요청. indirect(간접적)은 문맥상 약함.
det.tip: promote(홍보하다) ↔ neglect(방치하다) / direct(직접적인) ↔ indirect(간접적인)

questions.passage: My grandparents sell their delicious ①<u>organic</u> jam at the local market every weekend. I went to help them last weekend. However, they had already sold all of their jam! ✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ fewer(더 적은) → 원문은 more(더 많은). 온실을 지어서 딸기를 '더 많이' 기르려는 목적.

det.analysis:
✅ ①②③ 원문 그대로.
❌ ④ disappear(사라지다) → 원문은 spread(퍼지다). 캠페인 소식이 '퍼지는' 것이 맞음.

questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 당신은 또한 그 제품이 당신에게 얼마나 중요한지 표현해야 한다.
det.analysis: ✅ important: importance(명사) → important(형용사). how + 형용사 + S + V 감탄/의문 구조.
det.tip: importance(n. 중요성) → important(adj. 중요한) → importantly(adv. 중요하게)

questions.passage: My grandparents sell their delicious organic jam at the local market every weekend. I went to help them last weekend. However, they had already sold all of their jam! They didn't have enough strawberries to make any more jam. That evening, I sat by the window and stared out at the empty field behind their house. Suddenly, __________.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: ① I decided to give up

det.korean: 딸기가 부족해 잼을 더 만들 수 없었다. 빈 들판을 바라보던 중 갑자기 생각이 떠올랐다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② I got an idea: Suddenly 뒤에 아이디어가 떠오르는 전개.
❌ ① give up: 포기는 이후 크라우드펀딩 전개와 모순.
❌ ③ fell asleep: 갑자기 잠드는 것은 문맥과 무관.
❌ ④ called friends: 이후 전개와 무관.
det.tip: get an idea: 아이디어가 떠오르다 / Suddenly: 갑자기 (전환점 표시)

questions.passage: Funding for our campaign started slowly. When the first investor committed to supporting us, I almost jumped for joy. Now, after six weeks, we have raised almost $2,500. It seems like we might __________!
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 모금은 느리게 시작했다. 첫 투자자가 지원을 약속했을 때 기뻐서 뛰어올랐다. 6주가 지나 거의 $2,500를 모았다. 우리는 아마 재정 목표를 달성할 수도 있을 것 같다!
det.analysis:
✅ ③ make our funding goal: 목표 $5,000 중 $2,500 달성 → 목표 달성 가능성.
❌ ① lose investors: 기쁜 분위기와 반대.
❌ ② cancel: 잘 진행 중인데 취소는 모순.
❌ ④ start over: 다시 시작은 문맥과 맞지 않음.
det.tip: make a goal: 목표를 달성하다 / jump for joy: 기뻐서 뛰어오르다 / commit to ~ing: ~할 것을 약속하다
